h1: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte travel, stays & events guide
heroText: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte works best as a base in Sri Lanka when you anchor days around Parliament of Sri Lanka, Diyatha Uyana and Beddagana Wetland Park. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Colombo Ratmalana International Airport (RML) handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.label: 13th century
history.text: Here, in the 13th century, a local chieftain, Nissanka Alagakkonara, built a Kotte, or fortress.
The Portuguese arrived on the island in 1505 and were initially welcomed by the king, but they had militaristic and monopolistic intentions and gained control of the city by 1565.
While designated as the new capital in 1977 to relieve congestion in Colombo, the official relocation was marked by the inauguration of the new Parliament building in Kotte on 29 April 1982.
Sri Lanka formally changed its administrative capital from Colombo to Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte in 1982.
The Kotte Urban Council became the Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte Municipal Council in 1997, with Chandra Silva as the first Mayor.
